projects.name: Mise en Place
projects.tagline: AI that reads restaurant delivery notes
projects.role: Solo builder and owner: product, code, delivery and support
projects.description: A restaurant takes a photo of a supplier delivery note. The app reads the supplier, the dates and every line on it, then asks the owner to check only the bits it wasn't sure about. From there it turns into a daily to-do list sorted by how much money is on the line, a clear view of what they spend and on what, and price tracking that catches a supplier nudging prices up quietly. There are budgets, payment reminders, and a chat you can ask about your own buying history. Built in Spanish first, for independent restaurants and small groups.

highlights.title: When the reading goes wrong, it fails politely
highlights.body: If the PDF has real text in it, we read that. If it doesn't, we look at the image instead, and try again when the model has an off day. Every field comes back with a confidence score, so the owner only checks what's genuinely doubtful. Official e-invoices and VERI*FACTU QR codes skip the AI entirely: they already come structured, so there's nothing to guess at and nothing to pay for.

highlights.title: Comparing prices that aren't comparable
highlights.body: One supplier sells oil in a 5L garrafa, the next in a 12-pack, the next by the kilo. Every line gets broken down to a price per litre, per kilo or per unit. Without that, "this went up 8%" usually just means the box got smaller.

highlights.title: No restaurant can ever see another's data
highlights.body: Every table is tagged with the restaurant it belongs to, and every query has to go through the check that filters on it. An automated rule refuses to let the code ship if someone writes a query that skips that check, so the wall stays up as the app grows.

highlights.title: The slow work happens in the background
highlights.body: Reading a note takes a few seconds, so it runs in a queue instead of making anyone sit and wait. Anything that fails gets parked somewhere I can see it. Overnight the numbers are recalculated, and scheduled jobs send the weekly summary plus the nudges about unpaid invoices and trials running out.

highlights.title: Shipped like a product, not a demo
highlights.body: Real logins with email or Google, Stripe subscriptions where the plan you pay for is the plan you actually get, error tracking, rate limits, feature flags, and an admin view where I can see revenue, health and anything stuck. Restaurants can also just WhatsApp a photo of the note, which turned out to be the easiest way in.

projects.name: Glow Dental
projects.description: Software for running a dental clinic: appointments, patient records, billing and settings. The front end and the API share one set of typed definitions so they can't drift apart, and it was built test-first. The Next.js front end is done; the backend is the next piece.

projects.name: Automated Content Channel
projects.description: Takes a trending topic and turns it into a finished vertical video in five steps: spot the trend, write the script, plan the visuals, schedule the post, then check how it did. It runs itself once a day and hands back a shot-by-shot pack ready to film.

projects.name: BYD Interactive Presentation
projects.description: A presentation app for BYD's European sales training on the ATTO 2 DM-i. It runs full-screen on touchscreens at the venue, with navigation you can drive with a finger. I took it from the first client conversation through to the day it went live.

projects.name: Farmacia Granda
projects.description: An online shop for a neighbourhood pharmacy, built to load fast and stay easy for the owners to update.

projects.name: This portfolio
projects.description: The site you're on. No framework, no build step, just plain HTML, JavaScript and CSS. Every project and skill on the page comes from a single config file I edit by hand.

projects.name: Reelforge
projects.description: Turns trending data into vertical infographic videos on its own. The script, the voice and the final render each run as their own job, so one failure doesn't take the whole thing down with it.

projects.name: AutoAffiliate
projects.description: Writes product reviews with Claude and handles the unglamorous parts around them: SEO basics, affiliate links, and signing in to the platforms it posts to.
